consensus_summary: Primary meaning is a visible act, miracle, wonder, or token that points beyond itself to divine presence, power, purpose, or authenticates a messenger (esp. Jesus’ signs revealing identity); common alternatives are covenant markers, eschatological portents, prophetic sign-acts, and confirmatory tokens, with broad agreement on the pointing/authenticating function despite polyvalence.
book_summary: A prophecy given in advance—often a prophet’s lived story—whose fulfillment testifies; not a wonder performed on demand.
consensus_core_identification: Authenticating miracle/wonder or visible pointer to divine activity and identity
book_core_identification: Advance prophecy (often a prophet’s lived story) whose fulfillment testifies
boundary_disagreement: Book excludes on-demand wonders and authenticating miracles (consensus primary cases) from the category of sign, restricting the term to predictive prophecies and lived prophetic narratives whose later fulfillment serves as testimony.
material_contradiction: Book’s explicit denial that a sign is a wonder performed on demand directly opposes the consensus primary identification of signs as precisely such authenticating miracles/wonders.
rationale: Consensus cores (across all three responses) center on the authenticating miracle or visible pointer, treating prophetic sign-acts only as secondary alternatives. The book replaces that central referent with advance prophecy/lived story whose fulfillment testifies and expressly rejects the wonder-on-demand sense. This is replacement of the identification, not mere boundary adjustment of an intact category, even though a few shared examples (Isa 7:14, Ezekiel as sign, Jonah) survive under reclassification; hence DIVERGENT with CONTRADICTS at the core and partial reclassification of extension.
strongest_objection: Consensus already lists prophetic sign-acts and the sign of Jonah among common alternatives, so the book’s focus could be read as prioritization of one recognized sense rather than outright replacement of the polyvalent core.
